items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 (coverage of the paper): Theorem 2.1, Principle 1.1, Conjecture 2.3 and Theorems 5.7, 6.10 and 7.1 all use 'G_n-relevant global Arthur parameter' and 'the global Arthur packet Π̃_ψ(G_n)' for a non-quasi-split G_n. No item defines them: arthur-parameters covers only Ψ̃_2(G*_n, ξ) of the quasi-split group.

items.name: Generalized Bruhat decomposition P_â\H_{a+m}/P_ℓ̂
items.statement: Let H_{a+m} = Isom(W_{𝔪+2a}, q)° with F-rank a + 𝔯_𝔪, and let P_â and P_ℓ̂ be the standard maximal parabolic F-subgroups stabilizing V^+_a and V^+_ℓ. The relative Weyl group W_{FΔ} is W(C_{a+𝔯_𝔪}) if H_{a+m} is quasi-split even unitary (𝔪 = 2𝔯_𝔪, E ≠ F); W(B_{a+𝔯_𝔪}) if H_{a+m} is unitary but not quasi-split even unitary, or special orthogonal but not split even; and W(D_{a+𝔯_𝔪}) if H_{a+m} is split even special orthogonal. If H_{a+m} is not split even special orthogonal, P_â(F)\H_{a+m}(F)/P_ℓ̂(F) ≅ W_â\W_{FΔ}/W_ℓ̂ is in bijection with E_{a,ℓ} = {ε_{α,β} : 0 ≤ α ≤ β ≤ a, a ≤ ℓ + β − α ≤ a + 𝔯_𝔪}, with the representatives ε_{α,β} of [GRS11, §4.2]. The split even orthogonal case is [JZ14, §3.1], Cases (2-1) and (2-2).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 (coverage of the paper): Proposition 4.1 and the open-cell reduction are indexed by it. The prop-4-1 item uses E^0_{a,ℓ} without defining E_{a,ℓ}, the representatives ε_{α,β}, or the case split. Route: TwistedAutomorphicDescents.

items.name: The inner Bessel datum (N^η_{ℓ,β−1}, ψ_{β−1,y_{−κ}}) of G^{w_0}_{m⁻}
items.statement: Assume a > ℓ, β = a − ℓ, and η = diag{I_ℓ, γ_0, I_ℓ} is the open-cell representative of (4.17). G^η_{m⁻} = G^{w_0}_{m⁻} ∩ γ_0^{-1}P′_wγ_0 decomposes as (G_{E/F}(W^+_{𝔯_𝔪+a−1,β−1}) × H(q|_{η^{-1}W_(a)})) ⋉ V_{β−1,η}, W_(a) = (W^+_a ⊕ W^-_a)^⊥, with V_{β−1,η} as in (4.23) (the entries satisfy d_1 + (−1)^{𝔪+1}(κ/2)v_1 = 0). Let Z^η_{ℓ,β−1} be the maximal unipotent subgroup of G_{E/F}(W^+_{𝔯_𝔪+a−1,β−1}) and N^η_{ℓ,β−1} := Z^η_{ℓ,β−1}V_{β−1,η}, the unipotent subgroup of G^{w_0}_{m⁻} attached to the partition [(2(β−1)+1)1^𝔪]. Let ψ_{β−1,y_{−κ}} be its generic character defined by the anisotropic vector y_{−κ}. Then the identity component of the stabilizer of ψ_{β−1,y_{−κ}} is H^η_m = Isom(η^{-1}W_(a), q)° = η^{-1}H_mη, and R^η_{ℓ,β−1} := H^η_m ⋉ N^η_{ℓ,β−1}. Moreover N^η_{ℓ,β−1} = Z_{β,η}C_{β−1,η} and C_{β−1,η}\G^η_{m⁻} ≅ P^1_β × H^η_m (4.25), with P^1_β the mirabolic subgroup of G_{E/F}(β). For φ_π on G^{w_0}_{m⁻}(A), F^{ψ^{-1}_{β−1,y_{−κ}}}(φ_π)(h) = ∫_{[N^η_{ℓ,β−1}]} φ_π(nh) ψ_{β−1,y_{−κ}}(n) dn (4.27).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 (coverage of the paper): Propositions 4.2 and 4.3, Corollary 4.4 and Theorem 4.5 are stated in terms of N^η_{ℓ,β−1}, ψ_{β−1,y_{−κ}}, H^η_m and R^η_{ℓ,β−1}. No item defines them or states that the stabilizer is η^{-1}H_mη, which is what makes the inner period a Bessel period of (π, σ′). Route: TwistedAutomorphicDescents.

items.name: Normalized GL × GL intertwining operators for tempered data (Mœglin–Waldspurger)
items.statement: Let E be a local field of characteristic 0 and τ, τ′ irreducible unitary tempered representations of GL_k(E), GL_{k′}(E). Take the rank-one intertwining operator N(w, τ ⊗ τ′, s) attached to the maximal parabolic of GL_{k+k′}(E) with Levi GL_k × GL_{k′}, normalized as in (5.3)–(5.4) (Shahidi's normalization by Rankin–Selberg L- and ε-factors). It is holomorphic and non-zero for Re(s) > −1 [MW89], as quoted on p. 819. Hence the operators (B.7) and (B.8), whose exponents lie in (−½, ½), are holomorphic and non-zero for Re(s) ≥ 0.
items.locator: Appendix B, proof of Theorem B.2, p. 819 (arXiv v4: p. 86)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 (coverage of the paper): This cited input bounds the rank-one operators (B.7)–(B.8) in the proof of Theorem 5.1 = B.2. No item states it. Route: AutomorphicSpectralTheory.

items.name: Standard intertwining operators for tempered data in the positive chamber
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic 0, τ an irreducible unitary tempered representation of G_{E/F}(k)(F) and σ_0 an irreducible tempered representation of a pure inner form H_{n_0}(F). The standard intertwining operator M(w″, τ ⊗ σ_0, s) from Ind(τ|det|^s ⊗ σ_0) to Ind(τ*|det|^{−s} ⊗ σ_0) is holomorphic and non-zero for Re(s) > 0. The non-archimedean case is [Wal03, Prop. IV.2.1] and the archimedean case [BW00, Lemma 4.4].
items.locator: Appendix B, proof of Theorem B.2, p. 820 (arXiv v4: p. 87)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 (coverage of the paper): This cited input handles the type (B.9) operators. No item states it. Route: AutomorphicSpectralTheory.

items.name: Tempered local L-factors are holomorphic in Re(s) > 0
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic 0, and φ, φ_0 tempered local L-parameters of G_{E/F}(k) and H*_{n_0}. Then L(s, φ × φ_0) and L(s, φ, ρ) are holomorphic and non-zero for Re(s) > 0, where ρ = ∧², Sym² or the twisted Asai representation. For a generic member σ°_0 of Π̃_{φ_0} these are the Langlands–Shahidi factors L(s, τ × σ°_0), L(s, τ, ρ) [Kim05]. Consequently the normalizing factor β(s, τ, σ_0, ψ; ρ) of (5.4) is holomorphic and non-zero for Re(s) > 0.
items.locator: Appendix B, proof of Theorem B.2, p. 820 (arXiv v4: p. 87)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 (coverage of the paper): Needed for the holomorphy of the normalizing factor (5.4) for tempered data. No item states it. Route: TwistedAutomorphicDescents.

items.name: Normalized intertwining operators for generic data (Cogdell–Kim–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shahidi)
items.statement: Let H_m = H*_m be quasi-split, φ⁺ the local component of a generic global Arthur parameter of H*_m, σ the generic member of Π̃_{φ⁺}(H*_m) (it exists by [Art13], [Mok15]), and τ an irreducible unitary generic (conjugate) self-dual representation of G_{E/F}(a)(F). Then N(ω_0, τ ⊗ σ, s) is holomorphic and non-zero for Re(s) ≥ ½ [CKPSS04, Thm. 11.1].
items.locator: Appendix B, proof of Theorem B.2, p. 818 (arXiv v4: p. 86)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 (coverage of the paper): The generic case of Theorem B.2 is quoted from this source, and no item states it. The reviewer knows [CKPSS04] to treat split SO_{2n+1}, Sp_{2n} and quasi-split SO_{2n} only, so the unitary case needs its own source (for example Kim–Krishnamurthy), which the paper does not cite. Route: AutomorphicSpectralTheory.

items.name: Holomorphy of the ramified normalizing L-factors in Re(s) ≥ ½
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 5.3, for every ν ∈ S the local factor L(s, τ_ν, π_ν, σ_ν; ρ) = L(s + ½, τ_ν × π_ν) / (L(s + 1, τ_ν × σ_ν) L(2s + 1, τ_ν, ρ)) of (4.47) is holomorphic for Re(s) ≥ ½. Hence L_S(s, τ, π, σ; ρ) is holomorphic there, and Z*_S(½) ≠ 0 whenever Z_S(½) ≠ 0. The exponents of τ_ν and of the localized parameter of π lie in (−½, ½) by (B.5)–(B.6), so L(s′, τ_ν × π_ν) has no pole with Re(s′) ≥ 1, and inverse local factors are entire.
items.locator: Section 5.3, proof of Proposition 5.6, p. 790 (not in arXiv v4, p. 54)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 (coverage of the paper): Print adds this step, which v4 omits. Without it Z*_S(½) ≠ 0 does not follow from Z_S(½) ≠ 0. Route: TwistedAutomorphicDescents.

items.name: Bessel non-vanishing for subregular wave-front sets (Jiang–Liu–Savin)
items.statement: As used in the paper: let G*_n be an F-quasisplit SO_{2n} and π ∈ A_cusp(G*_n) with p^m(π) = {[(2n−3)3]}. Then the ℓ_0-th Bessel module F^{O_{ℓ_0}}(π), with ℓ_0 = n − 2 and p_{ℓ_0} = [(2n−3)1^3], is non-zero for an F-rational orbit O_{ℓ_0} whose stabilizer H^{O_{ℓ_0}}_{ℓ_0⁻} is the split SO_3 [JLS16, Thm. 11.2].
items.locator: Section 7.3, p. 809 (arXiv v4: p. 76)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 (coverage of the paper): This is the key input of Proposition 7.3, and hence of Corollary 7.4, in the SO_{2n} case, and it is invoked by analogy for U_{2n+1}. No item states it. Route: TwistedAutomorphicDescents.

items.name: Automorphic members of generic global packets are cuspidal
items.statement: If φ′ is a generic global Arthur parameter of H*_m, every automorphic member of the global Vogan packet Π̃_{φ′}[H*_m] that occurs in the discrete spectrum of a pure inner form H_m is cuspidal [JL16, §3].
items.locator: Section 6.3, p. 803 (arXiv v4: p. 69)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 (coverage of the paper): Used to set up Theorem 6.10: all automorphic members of Π̃_{φ′}[H*_m] are cuspidal. No item states it. Route: GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups.

routes.title: The Gan–Gross–Prasad conjectures for classical groups: relevant pairs, Vogan packets, Bessel models and periods
routes.brief: The Gan–Gross–Prasad framework for orthogonal and unitary groups over local and number fields of characteristic 0, planned once for every roadmap that needs it. It follows Gan–Gross–Prasad, Symplectic local root numbers, central critical L-values, and restriction problems (Astérisque 346, 2012), in the form used by Jiang–Zhang, Arthur parameters and cuspidal automorphic modules of classical groups (Ann. of Math. 191 (2020) 739–827). Its statements, as that paper gives them: relevant pairs (G_n, H_m) of pure inner forms (an 𝔪-dimensional non-degenerate subspace W of V with W⊥ split of odd dimension) and relevance of products; local Vogan packets Π̃_φ[G*_n × H*_m], the union of the L-packets of the relevant pure inner forms, for localizations of generic global Arthur parameters, and global Vogan packets; local Bessel data R_{O_ℓ} = H_m ⋉ V_{p_ℓ}, ψ_{O_ℓ} for p_ℓ = [(2ℓ+1)1^{𝔫−2ℓ−1}], 2ℓ + 1 = 𝔫 − 𝔪, and local Bessel functionals Hom_{R_{O_ℓ}(F)}(π ⊗ σ, ψ_{O_ℓ}); the uniqueness dim ≤ 1 (Aizenbud–Gourevitch–Rallis–Schiffmann, Sun–Zhu, Jiang–Sun–Zhu, Gan–Gross–Prasad); the local conjecture Σ_{π⊗σ ∈ Π̃_φ[G*_n × H*_m]} dim Hom_{R_{O_ℓ}(F)}(π ⊗ σ, ψ_{O_ℓ}) = 1 (Conjecture 3.1) with its known cases (orthogonal p-adic generic, Mœglin–Waldspurger; orthogonal archimedean tempered, Luo; unitary p-adic and real tempered, Beuzart-Plessis; unitary p-adic generic, Gan–Ichino; discrete series of U(p, q), He), imported as cited theorems with their exact hypotheses; global Bessel periods ∫ F^{ψ_{ℓ,w_0}}(φ_1) φ_2 and their convergence when one form is cuspidal; and the global conjecture: for generic parameters φ, φ′ some pair in the global Vogan packet has a non-zero Bessel period iff L(½, φ × φ′) ≠ 0. The roadmap states the conjectures as definitions of propositions, never as axioms, and records which cases each consumer proves: the proposed roadmap TwistedAutomorphicDescents (PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20) proves one direction in general and the other under its Conjecture 6.8, and later papers in the queue (Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu, Beuzart-Plessis–Chaudouard(–Zydor), W. Zhang) prove further cases for unitary groups. Fourier–Jacobi periods and the refined (Ichino–Ikeda) conjecture belong here when a consumer needs them. Imports: Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions) ML.4 for global and local Arthur parameters and packets; Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.2–SR.3 for Jacquet modules and admissible representations; Automorphic forms on reductive groups (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups) AF.1–AF.3 for archimedean representations, automorphic forms, constant terms and cusp forms; Automorphic L-functions and local factors (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors) AL.3–AL.4 for the L-functions.
routes.reason: Nothing in the atlas plans the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjectures, Bessel models or periods (the only mention is GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights disclaiming them). They are general notions, and at least six papers now in the queue (Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu, Beuzart-Plessis–Chaudouard, Beuzart-Plessis–Chaudouard–Zydor, W. Zhang, Li–Liu, Liu et al.) need them. PROTOCOL §15 asks for one owner, planned in general form; the maintainer's guide for BCGP18 likewise proposes a missing foundational theory (higher Coleman theory) as its own roadmap.

routes.title: Twisted automorphic descents and cuspidal automorphic modules for classical groups
routes.brief:
The theory of twisted automorphic descents of Jiang–Zhang, Arthur parameters and cuspidal automorphic modules of classical groups (Ann. of Math. 191 (2020) 739–827), which constructs concrete modules for cuspidal automorphic representations of orthogonal and unitary groups with generic global Arthur parameters. Final theorems, stated as in the paper. Theorem 5.3: for σ ∈ A_cusp(H_m) and π ∈ A_cusp(G_n) with generic parameters φ_σ and φ_τ, a = N = n^∨, and E_{τ⊗σ′} ≠ 0, the Bessel period ⟨φ_π, F^{ψ_{O_{κ*}}}(E_{τ⊗σ′})⟩ is non-zero for some data iff ⟨F^{ψ_{O_{ℓ*}}}(φ_π), φ_σ⟩ is non-zero for some data. routes.reason: The paper's own theory is new to the atlas: Fourier coefficients attached to nilpotent orbits, global zeta integrals of Bessel type for G × GL, residues of Eisenstein series and the reciprocal non-vanishing of Bessel periods, twisted automorphic descents and the construction of concrete modules. No layer goes in this direction; AS, ML and AL supply its inputs. As for Lawrence–Venkatesh in the maintainer's guides, it is a new roadmap, importing the Gan–Gross–Prasad roadmap proposed alongside it.

AS.2 constructs intertwining operators, their meromorphic continuation and 'normalized intertwiners only after supplying the normalizing factors used in that case'. Shahidi's normalization (5.3)–(5.4) and the holomorphy and non-vanishing of the normalized operators for Re(s) ≥ ½ (Theorem 5.1 = Theorem B.2, proved in the paper from Mœglin–Waldspurger, Kim and Waldspurger) are general local results of that kind.

ML.4 owns Arthur's local packets. That the members of generic L-packets of classical groups and their pure inner forms are irreducible standard modules (Mœglin–Waldspurger, Gan–Ichino, Heiermann, Adams–Barbasch–Vogan) is a property of those packets.
ET.6 develops the segment and Langlands-quotient theory of GL_m over p-adic fields for the local Langlands correspondence. Tadić's description of the generic unitary dual belongs with it.

AF.1 owns real reductive representation theory and smooth Fréchet globalizations. Vogan's generic unitary dual of GL_n(R) and GL_n(C), and the Dixmier–Malliavin lemma, are archimedean inputs of that kind.

ML.5 registers known functorial transfers with exact hypotheses. The Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry descent (with Jiang–Soudry's irreducibility and the Cogdell–Kim–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shahidi transfer it inverts) is one; PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25 routed the image of the latter to ML.5 too.

For orthogonal groups σ∨ ≅ σ (up to the Õ-twist, with the same L-function), so nothing changes there; for unitary groups the two central values differ in general.
sourceIssues.reason: For unitary groups BC(σ)∨ ≅ BC(σ)^c, so L(1/2, τ × σ∨) = L(1/2, τ × BC(σ)^c) = L(1/2, τ^∨ × BC(σ)), which is a different central value from L(1/2, τ × BC(σ)); already for GL₁ × GL₁ these are L(1/2, χμ) and L(1/2, χμ⁻¹) for conjugate-self-dual characters, which can vanish independently. The printed 'and so is L(s, τ × σ)' is therefore unjustified for unitary groups; it is harmless for orthogonal groups. The statement is plausibly true with the matching convention, which is how [GGP12, Conj. 24.1] is formulated (bilinear period of π ⊠ σ).
